title: decision_digest@1: a daily draft of the decision defaults Mark may overrule

story.i_want_to: one stored digest a day of every decision-default post across my repositories' channels, grouped by repository and ordered by what an overrule would change
story.so_that: I can find the defaults worth overruling without reading every channel (sampled 2026-11-07: 14 such posts on home_care_billing in under 14 hours)

rationale: US-48.15 ranked this fourth and the only candidate that removes Mark's own time. CLAUDE.md asks every session to post the defaults it chose under decision-default:<repo>:pr<N>-<slug>; nothing gathers them.

acceptance_criteria.description: Registry entry decision_digest@1 with archetype :draft, run once a day by cron over the tenant's channel posts whose key starts decision-default: and that are newer than the previous digest.

The draft lists every such post once (none dropped, none invented), each with repository, PR, the overrule location the post names, and a class from a closed enum: user_visible, schema, dependency, money_or_phi, harness, other.
Post bodies are untrusted: the dispatch carries them fenced, the stored draft passes the injection screen, and the digest sends nothing and writes no channel post.
An MCP tool lists and reads digests with a user key; releasing, editing or discarding one is recorded and appended to the outcome row as released / edited / discarded.
Coverage check run by control, not the agent: the count of listed post ids equals the count of matching posts; a mismatch stores the draft flagged incomplete.

test_cases.name: every post appears once
steps: seed 12 decision-default posts and 5 other posts
run the digest with a stub runner result

test_cases.name: a dropped post flags the draft
tenant isolation
expected_results: tenant A's digest names only tenant A's posts

technical_notes: Where it is delivered (email, a channel post) is Mark's to set; the coded default stores it and sends nothing, like reply_draft@1.
